themes.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning
themes.summary: Learning across devices with fewer communication rounds and smaller messages.
paragraphs: Communication is often a bottleneck when training a model across many devices. I study how local computation, compressed updates, and client sampling can reduce this cost while retaining convergence guarantees.
I study the trade-off between local computation and communication, and how to retain acceleration when only a subset of clients participates.
focus: Using local steps to reduce the number of communication rounds.
Reducing the size of transmitted updates while preserving convergence guarantees.
Supporting partial client participation in federated optimization.

papers.note: Uses local gradient steps to accelerate communication in federated optimization.
Extends accelerated local training to support client sampling.
Studies compressed gradient differences in methods based on random reshuffling.
Studies how variance reduction can lower total training cost when local computation is expensive.

themes.title: Privacy and Robustness
themes.summary: Protecting training data and learning reliably in the presence of faulty or malicious participants.
paragraphs: Keeping data on local devices does not, by itself, guarantee privacy, and distributed training must also account for faulty or malicious participants. I develop optimization methods with differential privacy and Byzantine-robustness guarantees.

I study how clipping, robust aggregation, local updates, and partial participation interact with convergence. Recent work also examines differential privacy for orthogonalized optimizers used in deep learning.
focus: Private federated learning with local updates and client sampling.
Understanding the effects of clipping and privacy noise on optimization.

papers.note: Combines Byzantine robustness with partial client participation through gradient-difference clipping.
Provides privacy and convergence guarantees while supporting local updates and partial participation.
Studies Byzantine robustness and differential privacy together under weaker assumptions.
Examines differentially private training with orthogonalized optimizer updates.

themes.title: Optimization for Deep Learning
themes.summary: Understanding and improving optimizers for training and adapting neural networks.
paragraphs: Training and adapting neural networks places demands on optimizer memory, update geometry, and parameter efficiency. I study algorithms that address these constraints alongside a theoretical analysis of their convergence.

This includes compressed adaptive optimizers, low-rank adaptation, sparsified training, and adaptive scaling for Muon. The aim is to connect practical training methods with a clearer understanding of when and why they converge.
focus: Reducing the memory cost of adaptive optimization.
Analyzing low-rank adaptation and sparsified training.
Adapting step scales in normalized optimizers.

papers.note: Reduces adaptive-optimizer memory overhead through compression and error feedback.
Develops a convergence framework for randomized low-rank adaptation.
Analyzes training formulations that sparsify both models and gradients.
Studies adaptive step scaling for Muon and related normalized optimizers.
